patternDescription: Compiler regex matches on "this spirit can't block" and emits unconditional SET_RESTRICTION CANNOT_BLOCK on self, dropping the relative BP filter ("Spirits with BP inferior to this Spirit's").

Target selection or removal operation (DESTROY/BOUNCE/TARGET) completely omits relative comparison constraints ("with BP equal or inferior to this Spirit's", "with cost equal or inferior to that Spirit's", etc.).

When "once per turn" is written as a sentence ("You can only use [Keyword] once per turn", "can only attack once per turn"), header_parser fails to extract it into header.limit, leaving the effect repeatable.
Loose regex matching on "can't be", "can't attack", or "can't block" emits an empty op { op: "COMBAT_RESTRICTION" } lacking target, condition, duration, or restriction mechanics.

Clause splitter regex strips "(This effect can't bring the number of cores on the opposing Spirit down to 0.)", allowing MOVE_CORE to completely deplete cores and illegally destroy spirits by core exhaustion.

Phrases establishing conditional prerequisite dependency ("When you've done so,", "If you do,") are not captured into clause.link, allowing secondary operations to execute even if the cost/prerequisite failed.
